newsitem.title: TOGO: Controversial Togo constitutional court installed.
newsitem.headline: Controversial Togo constitutional court installed.

text.p: Togo's President Gnassingbe Eyadema presided over the installation of the West African nation's new constitutional court on Saturday at a ceremony boycotted by the opposition.
The opposition shunned the ceremony in protest at the composition of the seven-member court, which was set up under the 1992 constitution.
Under the constitution, parliament nominates two seats, the president one and the prime minister one.

Given the current balance of power in Eyadema's favour in parliament and the government, the president or his supporters nominated all four. The remainder are a magistrates, a lawyer and a law professor all elected by their peers.
The seven judges, who took the oath of office individually, elected Atsou Koffi Amegah, a former head of the supreme court and former foreign minister, as president of the new court.
Terms range from three years for the political appointees to seven years from those from the profession.
